overloadMerges.note: The two doc syntax lines differ only in whether the leading '*' is passed (selecting whether object is a name-string vs. a Table/Variable/Field reference); collapsed into one overload. vPosition/hPosition form a nested optional pair (hPosition can only be passed together with vPosition) and the doc's second, trailing '*' is an independent optional literal flag (changes scrolling behavior when the target is already visible), modeled as its own optional param rather than left un-drafted.

params.name: asObjectName
params.description: If specified, object is an object name (string); if omitted, object is a table, a field, or a variable.

params.name: object
params.description: Object name (if * is specified) or Variable, Field, or Table (if * is omitted)

params.name: vPosition
params.description: Line number to display, or vertical scroll position in pixels (pictures); if omitted, scrolls only as needed to reveal the first highlighted line

params.name: hPosition
params.description: Column number to display (list box), or horizontal scroll position in pixels (pictures); can only be passed together with vPosition

params.name: scrollToFirstPosition
params.description: Trailing '*'. If present, forces the target line (and column, if hPosition is passed) to be placed in the first visible position even if it was already visible; for pictures, places the requested point at the picture's origin (0,0) even if already shown.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Scrolls the visible content (rows/columns of a subform, list form, hierarchical list, or list box; or the pixel offset of a picture) of the object(s) designated by object and * to the position given by vPosition/hPosition, or, if these are omitted, auto-scrolls just enough to reveal the first highlighted line.

jointConstraints.rule: hPosition can only be passed if vPosition is also passed, since it is nested inside vPosition's optional group in the signature.

This trailing '*' only changes behavior when the target line/column (given by vPosition/hPosition) would otherwise already be visible and the command would do nothing; for pictures it forces the requested point to the origin (0,0) even if already shown.

constraints: Uses the list box's 'standard' (non-hierarchical) row numbering for vPosition even when the list box is displayed in hierarchical mode, so results can differ between standard and hierarchical display.
For pictures, the object must be displayed in the 'Truncated (non-centered)' format for vPosition/hPosition to apply.
The HIGHLIGHT RECORDS command has its own optional * parameter that can delegate scroll management to this command.
